answers.core: Part of RPCs, impossible to mod RPCs.
answers.workaround: Yes, because interface can always be replaced with a child node with a class that does the interface functionality by itself. But this means secondhand access everywhere (ex. `MyClass.DamageTaker.TakeDamage(...)` over `MyClass.TakeDamage(...)`).

title: Allow interface functions to be invoked by RPCs
